---
title: LaunchedEffect and rememberCoroutineScope
version: 1
---

**A composable must never start work in its body**, because its body runs whenever Compose decides
to recompose it, which may be many times a second or not at all. Lesson 3 called these the functions
that should not. A coroutine started there would start again at every recomposition. Compose gives
two places where a coroutine may start instead, and `WeekRoute` uses both.

## `LaunchedEffect`: work that belongs to being on screen

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(viewModel) {
    viewModel.events.collect { event -> … }
}
```

`LaunchedEffect` starts its block in a coroutine when the composable enters the composition, and
cancels it when the composable leaves. **The key decides restarts**: if `viewModel` were ever a
different object, the old coroutine would be cancelled and a new one started for the new key. With
`Unit` as the key it would run once and never restart, which is right only when nothing it reads can
change. Here the key is the ViewModel, so the collector always listens to the one the screen draws.

## `rememberCoroutineScope`: work started by a click

A click handler is not composition: it runs once, when the student taps, and may want to call a
`suspend` function. `showSnackbar` is one, since it suspends until the snackbar is dismissed.
`rememberCoroutineScope()` returns a scope tied to the composable's place in the composition, and
`scope.launch` from the click starts the work there. When the composable leaves, the scope is
cancelled, and so is any snackbar it was still showing. The total's `onTotalClick` does exactly that,
and involves no ViewModel: converting 160 minutes to hours is a matter of the screen.

| | starts | cancelled | use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LaunchedEffect(key)` | on entering composition, and when the key changes | on leaving, or on a new key | collecting, a timer, anything that runs because the screen is there |
| `rememberCoroutineScope()` | when you call `launch`, from a callback | on leaving composition | a suspend call caused by the student, such as a snackbar or a scroll |

## Seeing the result

This test types 45 and presses **Add**, waits until the snackbar the `LaunchedEffect` showed is on
screen, and saves the screen:

```kotlin
// app/src/test/java/com/example/planner/SnackbarTest.kt
package com.example.planner

import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createAndroidComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onAllNodesWithText
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithText
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onRoot
import androidx.compose.ui.test.performClick
import androidx.compose.ui.test.performTextInput
import com.github.takahirom.roborazzi.captureRoboImage
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
@Config(qualifiers = "w360dp-h400dp-xhdpi")
class SnackbarTest {
    @get:Rule val rule = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    @Test fun addingShowsASnackbar() {
        rule.onNodeWithText("Minutes").performTextInput("45")
        rule.onNodeWithText("Add").performClick()
        rule.waitUntil(5_000) { rule.onAllNodesWithText("Added 45 min").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        rule.mainClock.advanceTimeBy(1_000)
        rule.onRoot().captureRoboImage("screenshots/added.png")
    }
}
```

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ ./gradlew --console=plain testDebugUnitTest --tests '*SnackbarTest' -Proborazzi.test.record=true 2>&1 | grep -E "^(BUILD|[0-9]+ actionable)|PASSED|FAILED|^    [a-z]"
SnackbarTest > addingShowsASnackbar PASSED
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 12s
31 actionable tasks: 2 executed, 29 up-to-date
```

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "The week screen after adding a session: \"45 min this week, 0 of 1 done\", an empty Minutes field with the Add button disabled, one unticked session dated 2026-10-30 at 45 minutes, and a dark snackbar at the bottom reading \"Added 45 min\".", "caption": "SnackbarTest after pressing Add: the state from the store, and the one-off event as a snackbar. The date is the day the test ran."}
```

The session is in the list, the field is empty again, and the snackbar at the bottom names the
minutes the event carried.
